load_rejected_preflight.reason: Including native Player header in executable probe emitted an unresolved RakNet SystemAddress constructor. Loader rejected the plugin before enable. No fourth-hook test or player connection occurred in that startup. Corrected executable uses independently compiled field ABI; full Player header is confined to LLVM layout fixture.

native_abi.evidence: Four embedded request-processing diagnostic string references converge on the same ELF FDE. Three disassembled native callers tail-jump with this in RDI. The callee consumes no other live input register and returns void. This is binary-derived ABI; no declaration for this manager exists in the pinned public SDK.
native_abi.field_verification: Actual pinned Player header independently compiled to LLVM, then live field dereference admitted only after readable range and exact native manager vtable checks.
native_abi.queue_layout: Native callee reads size at144 and start at136. Independent libc++ deque fixture gives48-byte deque and size at40, consistent with native queue base104.
native_abi.operation: For the watched native manager with a nonempty queue, increment request revision on entry and exit, maintain active depth through RAII, and forward the original function. Empty queues do not invalidate. Previous save/change/set hooks retained.

after_vanilla_extraction_before_cursor_r.cursor: Six extracted stones on the native client cursor, excluded from the36-slot native inventory snapshot.

limitations: Private native diagnostic, not a new public SDK lock or editor API.
Detects the tested queued client bundle edit; does not qualify every direct component mutator, native plugin edit or multiplayer interleaving.
No request cancellation, item reservation, save suppression, partial-write barrier, rollback or crash recovery.
An in-flight revision/depth observation must become part of admission and commit revalidation before it can authorize writes.
No Windows ABI or runtime inference; all catalog acceptance flags remain unqualified.
Raw account data, worlds, item/book NBT and disassembly stay private.
